projects.title: Bratwurst-Reheated
projects.readme: # Bratwurst Reheated A fan remake of the Amiga shooter **Bratwurst**, built in GameMaker Studio 1.4 as a stand-alone Windows game. Float, shoot, crash and repeat, with one to four players, keyboard and Xbox controllers, and a terminal-style look with 34 colour themes and a team mode, Capture the Bratwurst. The goal is to keep the feel and the physics of the original wherever it can be verified, and then grow it with new maps, game modes, ships, weapons and music. ## What's new ### UPDATE 57 - 2026-11-10 - Super Smashwurst: Push Strength - New setting PUSH STRENGTH in the Super Smashwurst menu. It sets how hard a hit throws a ship, without changing the Push percentage. 5 is normal (100%), every step up adds 20% more knockback and every step down takes 20% away. At 10 (200%) a ship with 100% Push is thrown twice as far. ### UPDATE 56 - 2026-11-09 - Missiles hit the whole ship - Missiles (normal, guided and Mini Nuke) now hit as soon as they touch any of the lines that make up a ship. Before, a fast missile could slip straight through a ship or you had to hit almost the exact middle. Cannon shots work as before. ### UPDATE 55 - 2026-11-08 - New game mode: Super Smashwurst - Game Modes -> SUPER SMASHWURST is a new last-ship-standing mode for 2 to 4 players, inspired by Super Smash Bros. There is no energy bar. Every hit raises the Push percentage of the ship that was hit (a cannon shot +1%, a missile +10%), and the higher the Push, the farther a hit throws the ship. At 0% a hit does not move you at all, at 100% or more it can launch you far outside the arena. - The red arena boundary no longer stops you: ships, shots and missiles fly straight through it. Once a ship is outside, it gets its own countdown (5 seconds by default) next to the ship. Fly back inside in time and the countdown is cancelled; fly out again and a new one starts. When it reaches zero the ship explodes and you lose a life. - Everyone starts with 3 lives. At zero lives you are out. The last ship standing wins the round; if everyone is out at once it is a draw. - Each player's panel shows PUSH in a colour that goes from blue to red as it rises, plus the lives left. Settings: STARTING LIVES, OUT-OF-BOUNDS TIME, CANNON PUSH and MISSILE PUSH, along with players, map, rounds and powerups (off by default). Guided missiles, Mini Nukes and the railgun count as missiles. - The default map is Proxima Merguez. You can pick any other Classic map on the MAP row. - This is a first version that is still being tested, so the knockback feel may change. ### UPDATE 54 - 2026-11-07 - Capture the Bratwurst: missiles knock the sausage loose - If you carry the sausage and get hit by a missile (a direct hit, the red explosion ring, a guided missile or a Mini Nuke), you drop it. The sausage keeps its speed and either team can grab it, but you cannot pick it up again for one second. - Cannon shots and the railgun still only make the sausage spin extra fast. A missile from a teammate does nothing, as before. ### UPDATE 53 - 2026-11-06 - Capture the Bratwurst, first playable version - Game Modes -> CAPTURE THE BRATWURST is now a real game mode. Choose PLAYERS (2 to 4), MAP, ROUNDS, SCORE LIMIT (default 5 points), TIME LIMIT (default 5 minutes) and POWERUPS. START checks that the map has a sausage spawn and both zones. - One sausage, two teams. Fly close to the sausage to pick it up; it trails softly behind you. Carry it into the OTHER team's zone to score one point. Your own zone never scores. - After a point: RED or BLUE TEAM SCORES for 3 seconds, then a big countdown 3, 2, 1, and the sausage grows back at its spawn. The round timer keeps running and ships can still fly and shoot, but the sausage cannot be picked up until it is back. - Hit the carrier and the sausage spins extra fast for a second. If the carrier is destroyed the sausage is dropped, keeps its speed, slows down and bounces off walls, and either team can grab it. - Teammates cannot hurt each other: shots, missiles, explosions and the railgun pass through them. - A round ends at the score limit or when the time runs out. Most points wins; if the points are level, the team that carried the sausage longest wins; if that is level too, it is a draw. - The round result shows the winning team, the score, kills (most kills marked) and the carry time of every player. After the last round you see the match result with round wins per team. Kills are statistics only and never give points. - This is a first version that is still being tested, so the feel (sausage speed, pick-up distance) may change. ### UPDATE 52 - 2026-11-04 - Capture the Bratwurst: map editor and teams - The map editor has three new tools for Capture the Bratwurst: C places the sausage spawn (one per map), R draws the red team's zone and V draws the blue team's zone. The zones are not solid, ships fly straight through them. Everything is saved with the map. - The editor shows CTB READY, or what is missing, and warns when you save a Capture the Bratwurst map that is not finished. - Capture the Bratwurst only lists maps that were saved for it. Older maps no longer show up there by mistake. - Two teams: P1 and P3 are red, P2 and P4 are blue. The team colours are taken from the colour theme. ### UPDATE 51 - 2026-10-28 - Galaxy Duel damage flash - A damaged ship in Galaxy Duel now flashes quickly in three colours from the theme until it is repaired, so you can see at a glance who is hurt. - The damage now lasts 4 seconds instead of 6. ### UPDATE 50 - 2026-10-25 - Chromostereopsis themes - Four new colour themes: ChromostereopsisX2, X4, X6 and X8. They use a pure black background with red for things that should look close (walls, shots, explosions) and blue for things that should look far away (ships, text, dots). Many people see red as closer than blue, which gives a feeling of depth with colour alone. - X2 uses only pure red and pure blue. X4, X6 and X8 add more shades close to those colours. - There are now 34 colour themes. ### UPDATE 49 - 2026-10-20 - Ship select - On the ship select screen every ship is now scaled automatically so it fits inside the radar circle, also when it rotates. The big ships no longer stick out of the frame. - The ship name is no longer shown inside the picture (it is still on the SHIP row). ### UPDATE 48 - 2026-10-20 - New font - The whole game now uses the Rodchenko Light font (by ParaType), a thin constructivist-style typeface, with smooth edges. Small text, menu choices and headings use three sizes. - The temporary FONT TEST page in Options is gone again. ### UPDATE 47 - 2026-10-20 - Map editor in the main menu, font test - The MAP EDITOR is now in the main menu, right under CONTROLS, instead of in Options. - A temporary FONT TEST page in Options shows several fonts in different sizes, with and without anti-aliasing, so a new font can be picked. ### UPDATE 46 - 2026-10-19 - New pause menu - The pause menu is now a band across the screen: PAUSED on top, the choices (RESUME, OPTIONS, QUIT TO MENU) on one row, a line with match info, small player cards below and a button help row. - Press Y (or C on the keyboard) to see the controls. Left and right (or up and down) change the choice. - The button help row uses square boxes with the letter centered in each box. ### UPDATE 45 - 2026-10-19 - Explosion knockback - Explosions now push ships away. When the red ring from a missile, a guided missile or a Mini Nuke reaches a ship, the ship is thrown away from the centre of the explosion, hardest close to the centre. - The missile knockback is strong by default. Both the missile and the Mini Nuke have a BLAST KNOCKBACK setting in the secret Powerup Editor (0 turns it off). ### UPDATE 44 - 2026-10-18 - Missile blast and weapon settings - The red ring from a missile explosion now hurts as much as a direct hit (12 energy for a missile, 5 for a guided missile). A ship that is hit directly does not take both. - The secret Powerup Editor (press P in Options) has two new pages: CANNON (damage, shot speed, gravity, reload time, knockback) and MISSILE (speed, explosion time, direct damage, blast damage, blast radius, damage radius, particles, knockback, cooldown). - The missile explosion ring has a fixed size on the map now, so it no longer changes with the camera zoom. ### UPDATE 43 - 2026-10-18 - Tidier HUD, fading arena edge, countdown sound - Player panels: the ship now sits alone in the middle of the right side, smaller, with the numbers in the corners: position (Race) or round at the top left, wins at the top right, and laps or lives with small boxes along the bottom. In Galaxy Duel a damaged ship shows its repair time. - The outer edge of the arena fades in when a ship gets close to it and disappears when you are far away. - The Race countdown (3, 2, 1, GO!) now has a sound. ### UPDATE 42 - 2026-10-18 - LCD countdown - The Race countdown (3, 2, 1, GO!) is now drawn like a digital LCD display with straight segments and no rounded corners. ### UPDATE 41 - 2026-10-18 - Sliding along walls - Ships no longer get stuck on walls. When you hit a wall you now slide along it and slow down. The more the nose points into the wall, the more you slow down, and you can turn away and keep flying. - Sparks fly from the ship while it scrapes along a wall. - Wall damage now depends on how hard you hit the wall head-on, so scraping along a wall hardly hurts. ### UPDATE 40 - 2026-10-18 - Race maps and countdown - Race now only lists maps that were saved with Race ticked in the map editor. If there are none, the map row says NO RACE MAPS and START is locked. New maps start as Classic and Galaxy Duel only. Older maps without a finish box lose their Race mark once. - The 3, 2, 1, GO! countdown is drawn with sharp vector lines instead of a stretched font. ### UPDATE 39 - 2026-10-18 - Map editor tools - The map editor tool panel is tidier: smaller text and the tools are split into STATUS, DRAW, PLACE, VIEW and FILE, each in its own colour. The active tool is highlighted and the help line at the bottom follows the tool. - Zoom in and out with the mouse wheel (it zooms around the mouse pointer). Hold SPACE and drag with the mouse (or drag with the middle button) to move around when zoomed in. HOME resets the view. - Over the finish box the wheel still turns the arrows. ### UPDATE 38 - 2026-10-18 - Race countdown - Race starts with a big countdown in the middle of the screen: 3, 2, 1, GO! You cannot thrust until GO!, and the race time starts then. - Fullscreen: the Windows key no longer makes the game flicker out and back in. Alt+Tab still leaves fullscreen right away. ### UPDATE 37 - 2026-10-18 - Race positions and results - Race position: the panel shows POS x / N. It depends on finished ships, laps, who crossed the finish box first and the start order. - Pickups now depend on your position: the leader only gets a plasma shot, the middle gets plasma or a missile, and last place gets a guided missile or drift fuel. - Ships that have finished fly on as ghosts: they cannot shoot, collide or be hit. - When only one racer is left, it has 4 seconds to finish (ELIMINATED IN 4, 3, 2, 1) or its ship explodes. - Race result screen with the winner, places and times, and PRESS TO ENTER NEXT RACE. The winner gets a round win. ### UPDATE 36 - 2026-10-18 - Race pickups - Race pickups: round orange balls on the course. Fly into one to get a single plasma shot, a missile, a guided missile or a full drift fuel meter. The weapon is selected for you. The ball comes back after 5 seconds. - Map editor: new tool O places, moves and (with X) removes pickup points, up to 16 per map. - For now the pickup you get is random. Soon it will depend on your race position. ### UPDATE 35 - 2026-10-18 - Race weapons - In Race everyone starts with no ammo and no drift. The cannon uses one ammo per shot, and drift fuel does not recharge on its own. - Weapons no longer damage or kill in Race. A hit makes the ship 80% slower for 3 seconds (a new hit restarts the time). The player panel shows the slow time as SL. - Pickups that give ammo and drift are still to come. ### UPDATE 34 - 2026-10-18 - Race (first part) - New game mode: RACE. Pick laps, map, rounds and powerups (off by default) in the menu. The player panel shows your lap and the top bar shows the race time. - Map editor: new tool F draws a start/finish box. The box has arrows for the racing direction (turn them with the mouse wheel), and ships fly straight through it. Cross it in the arrow direction to finish a lap. Race maps without a finish box show a warning. - Hitting a wall no longer damages your ship in Race. - Race is not finished yet: no pickups or weapon rules and no race results screen. ### UPDATE 33 - 2026-10-18 - Drifting fuel - Drifting now uses fuel. A full meter gives 8 seconds of drift. Fuel is only used while you drift, and what is left is kept for later. - When the meter is empty it recharges in exactly 6 seconds, and you cannot drift until it is full. - The player panel shows the meter as AB (blue, red while recharging) instead of RF LOCKED. - The length can be changed in the hidden Powerup Editor (P in Options) under DRIFT: DRIFTING FUEL. ### UPDATE 32 - 2026-10-18 - Galaxy Duel - Astro Duel is now called GALAXY DUEL. - A hit no longer kills right away. The first hit damages your ship for 4 seconds: it is 60% slower and you cannot use any weapons, only steer and thrust. Sparks fly from the ship and little pieces fall off, and the ship flashes in three theme colours. After 4 seconds it is repaired and works like new. - If you are hit while damaged, your ship explodes. ### UPDATE 31 - 2026-10-16 - Alt-tab in fullscreen - Another fix for the window disappearing when you alt-tab out of FULLSCREEN: the game now leaves fullscreen as soon as you press Alt+Tab or the Windows key, and returns when you come back. ### UPDATE 30 - 2026-10-16 - Title screen credits - The title screen has a credits line at the bottom: Bratwurst (1995) originally fried by Three Little Elks (3LE) and Reheated (2026) by Thermoptic. - The ESC = QUIT text is gone from the title screen. ### UPDATE 29 - 2026-10-15 - Pause menu music - The pause menu now lets you change song with LB / RB. - The pause menu only shows gamepad controls (the keyboard list is gone). - Options: WINDOW is renamed SCREEN MODE. ### UPDATE 28 - 2026-10-15 - Cleaner options - Options: WIDE PLAYFIELD is gone (the playfield is always wide). SCANLINES and PHOSPHOR GLOW are now one switch: SCANLINES AND GLOW. - The MUSIC on/off row is gone. VOLUME now goes down to 0%, shown as OFF, which turns the music off. - The DATA box in the main menu shows the description right at the top, without the INFO heading. ### UPDATE 27 - 2026-10-15 - Asteroids, zoom and polish - New game mode: ASTEROIDS. Waves of rocks fly in from the edges; shoot them and they split into smaller, faster ones. Options has a LEVEL setting (1 to 5, default 3) where every level doubles everything. - New option ZOOM (1 to 10): 1 is the normal camera, 10 shows twice as much of the arena. It changes smoothly and works in every game mode. - A seventh song: Juke to Jupiter. The music fades in when the game starts. - The music player buttons are lined up (plus and minus in line with play/pause, MUTE under next). Panels get corner brackets. - Title screen says PRESS START TO TURN UP THE HEAT. - Alt-tab from fullscreen no longer makes the window disappear. - Your own shots no longer hit you when you fire straight ahead at full speed. ### UPDATE 26 - 2026-10-14 - Smaller music files - The five songs are re-encoded at a slightly lower quality, so the game is about 4 MB smaller (the music is about 15 MB instead of 19 MB). Length and the equalizer are unchanged. ### UPDATE 25 - 2026-10-14 - Music player in the main menu - The right side of the main menu is now two boxes: DATA on top and a MUSIC player below it. The player has the spectrum, the song name and number, a timeline with elapsed and remaining time, previous / play-pause / next buttons, shuffle, repeat, volume (minus, LED bar, plus), a MUTE button and the next track at the bottom. - Everything in the player can be clicked with the mouse; click the timeline to seek. LB / RB change song, Y (or M on the keyboard) plays and pauses. - Songs no longer loop forever: when a song ends the next one starts (shuffle picks a random one, repeat plays the same). The title song still loops on the title screen. - The Palette and Files boxes are gone to make room. ### UPDATE 24 - 2026-10-14 - Navigation dots, safer shots - Navigation dots: a fixed grid of coloured pixels, 100 pixels apart, covers the whole arena so you can tell where you are and how fast you move when nothing else is in view. They only show when the camera is zoomed in and fade out completely when it zooms out. - Shots and missiles now get the forward speed of your ship on top of their own speed (in the direction you fire), so a fast ship at full speed can no longer fly into its own shots. They still go exactly where the nose points. - Solid colors: the fill now covers the whole hull, with no thin edge next to the outline. ### UPDATE 23 - 2026-10-14 - Solid colors, side thruster, B to go back - New option SOLID COLORS (Options, OFF by default): fills all solid walls and the ships with their colour. - Drift: new SIDE THRUSTER setting (secret Powerup Editor, DRIFT page). While you drift, thrust and turn, a side thruster pushes the ship out of the curve (turn right = pushed left, turn left = pushed right), like a rally car sliding through a corner. - B on the gamepad goes back one step on the ship select screen (and back to the menu from the first row). - Fixed a crash when the camera zoomed after a ship was destroyed. ### UPDATE 22 - 2026-10-14 - New icon, Dracula theme - The game has a new icon: the BW logo with the equalizer ring. - Dracula is now the default theme. A theme you pick is still saved and used next time. - The debug text in the top left of the play area is hidden by default. Press F1 to show it. ### UPDATE 21 - 2026-10-14 - Options in the pause menu, drift settings - The pause menu has a new OPTIONS entry. It opens the normal options menu on top of the match, so you can change theme, volume and so on while you play. Esc goes back to the pause menu. - The secret Powerup Editor (Options, press P) has a new DRIFT page with every setting for drifting and reversing: start speed, turn boost, slide angle, drift thrust, reverse thrust, trail length, engine sound and trail width. ### UPDATE 20 - 2026-10-14 - Smooth camera zoom - When a player dies (or comes back after respawning) the camera no longer jumps straight to the players that are left. It zooms and moves smoothly, in about a second. ### UPDATE 19 - 2026-10-14 - Railgun - New powerup: RAILGUN. Pick it up and hold the powerup button (B) for 4 seconds. A glowing ball grows in front of the ship and turns white when it is charged. Let go to fire: a beam in your colour shoots through the whole map, over every wall and object, reaches the other side in half a second, stays for 2 seconds and fades out in 1. It kills a ship in one hit. - Sounds: a wobbling charge-up sound that grows stronger and higher while you charge, a ready sound when the Railgun is charged, and a powerful sci-fi laser sound when it fires. Hold the button for 3 seconds after it is charged and it fires by itself. Let go too early and nothing is fired. - The Powerup Editor has a Railgun page with charge time, beam speed, hold and fade time, beam width, damage, camera shake and ball size. - The title song now keeps playing when you go from the title screen to the main menu. ### UPDATE 18 - 2026-10-14 - Powerups: Mini Nuke - New powerup system. A rotating, colour-cycling orb with an icon appears on the map 5 seconds after a round starts, on a random spot away from walls and objects. Fly into it to pick up the powerup. A new one appears 10 seconds after one is picked up. - First powerup: MINI NUKE. Press B on the gamepad to fire it: a big glowing projectile that explodes with a growing shockwave, a cloud of pixel particles and a camera shake. - Game modes: new POWERUPS ON/OFF setting for Classic and Astro Duel (default ON). - Secret Powerup Editor: open Options and press P. Set projectile size, speed, shockwave radius, particles, damage and camera shake for every powerup. - Music: the title song (3LE - Das Bratwurst, DnB edit) now plays on the title screen only. Menus and matches play the other songs. - Gamepad: Y fires the special weapon, B fires the powerup, Back switches special weapon. The button that cycled the number of players is gone. - New pause menu with match stats and a list of all controls. ### UPDATE 17 - 2026-10-14 - Sausage, drift sound, round win text - A wireframe sausage (for the future Capture the Bratwurst mode) now drifts and rotates in the background of the title screen and menu together with the ships. The model is drawn as an SVG that you can edit yourself (assets/models). - Drift has its own sound: a looping spaceship engine that plays as long as you drift. - When a round is won the screen says WELL HOT DOG, WE HAVE A WEINER! with the winning player underneath. - New LIFE setting for Classic (1 to 6 lives, 6 is the default and the maximum). - The outer line of the arena frame is gone on all maps (your own maps are updated automatically, with a backup). - Ship select: PRESS FIRE TO JOIN blinks on every open slot. ### UPDATE 16 - 2026-10-14 - New pause menu, new gamepad layout - New pause menu: a compact PAUSED box in the middle, a MATCH STATS box on the left (mode, round, map, song, time, players, leader, and for every player the ship, wins, lives and energy) and a CONTROLS box on the right that lists what every button does. - Gamepad: Special weapon is now on Y, Next special weapon on Back. The "cycle number of players" button is gone (join players on the ship select screen or choose Players in the menu). ### UPDATE 15 - 2026-10-14 - Glowing missiles, shots go where you aim - All missiles are now a glowing ball with a solid core that pulses and flickers, with small pixel particles flying out behind it. - Shots and missiles always fire exactly in the direction the ship is pointing, even when you drift or slide sideways at full speed. They no longer inherit the speed of your ship. ### UPDATE 14 - 2026-10-14 - Drift light trails - Drifting now leaves light trails behind the ship in the colour of the ship: two trails for wide ships, one for narrow ones. The trails grow out as you start to drift, follow the path you move along and fade out towards the tail. When you stop drifting the whole trail fades away. - A glowing ball sits where each trail starts, to show that the engine is working: a solid core with a soft glow that pulses and flickers. - Drift slides more to the side and has stronger thrust. The trails are thinner and half as long, and the trail keeps hanging on the ship while it fades out when you let go of the drift button. ### UPDATE 13 - 2026-10-14 - Pause menu, drift and reverse - Pause menu: press Esc or Start during a match for Resume Game and Quit to Menu. The game stands still while it is open. - Drifting (new, experimental): hold the left trigger while you thrust to slide sideways. Faster turning, thrust pushed outwards from the turn, sparks behind the ship. It only works while you thrust and move. Special weapon switch moved from the left trigger to Y. - Reverse: press only the left trigger (no thrust) to back the ship up very slowly, for example out of a wall. - Missile explosions are 30 percent bigger when the missile hits a wall or a player. - Ship select: every open slot shows a smaller, centred PRESS FIRE TO JOIN, also slot 4. - Music: five Thermoptic tracks added to the playlist, music plays during matches (a new random song every round, shown in the top bar), and a Volume setting in Options (10 to 100 percent, default 70). ### UPDATE 12 - 2026-10-14 - Music playlist, camera lock - The main menu shows NOW PLAYING with the name of the current song under the spectrum. Press LB / RB on a gamepad (or PageUp / PageDown) on the title screen, in the menu or on ship select to switch song. - Six songs in the playlist: 3LE - Das Bratwurst (DnB edit, played on the title screen only) and five Thermoptic tracks (No Safe Orbit, Sectorwurst, We Were Never Organic - Disco Edit, Nothing Good Beyond Neptune, The Final Frankfurter). The spectrum follows each song, and long titles scroll. - Music now plays during matches too: a random song starts every round and its name is shown in the top bar. New Volume setting in Options (10 to 100 percent, default 70). - When only one player is left the camera stays where it is instead of zooming in on the winner. - The map name is part of the header line during a match. ### UPDATE 11 - 2026-10-14 - Ship select redesign, respawn countdown, bigger explosions - New ship select screen: every player pane is divided into a step strip, a numbered row list, weapon chips, a framed rotating ship with radar rings, and stat bars (speed, energy, turn, ammo, rate). Up/Down changes the row, Left/Right changes the value. - Respawn: after losing a life the ship waits 3 seconds. The player panel shows 3, 2, 1 and then the ship spawns as usual. - Missile explosions are twice as big, with a large cloud of pixel particles. The expanding ring now hurts ships it reaches: 3 energy, once per explosion (Classic). - Sparks when ships crash into each other and when shots hit walls. Ramming a ship now pushes and slightly twists it depending on speed and where you hit, and ships that overlap are pushed apart so they cannot get stuck. - Map editor: Load Map window (L) with a table of which game modes each map is made for. - The main menu shows a picture of the selected map on the MAP row. The map name is shown in the header while you play. ### UPDATE 10 - 2026-10-14 - Maps per game mode, menu spectrum - Map editor save window: type a name (or press Generate name for a random star-and-sausage name) and tick the game modes where the map should be available. - The map list in each game mode only shows the maps made for that mode. Classic and Astro Duel now have their own map choice. - Rotate a start position in the map editor with the mouse wheel. - The main menu has the same background as the title screen: grid, twinkling stars and drifting ships. - New spectrum visualizer in the menu: 32 bars, falling peaks, a mirror image, an oscilloscope line and a short history strip. It follows the music and uses the colours of the selected theme. - After the last opponent is destroyed there are 4 more seconds of play before the round result appears. ### UPDATE 9 - 2026-10-13 - New title screen, no gravity - New title screen: a centred line logo, a circular equalizer ring around it that dances to the music, pulsing planets, twinkling stars and the drifting ships in the background. - Ships no longer sink when you let go of the controls. A ship you are not steering stands completely still. ### UPDATE 8 - 2026-10-13 - Astro Duel - New game mode: ASTRO DUEL. Every hit costs a life (default 1 life, so one hit kills). Choose 1-9 lives. - No damage from crashing into walls. - Only 3 shots, then a 4 second reload. Fire them as fast or as slow as you like. - Bigger projectiles (30 percent) that are easier to hit with. - Only Missile (twice as fast) and Turbo Boost, for every ship. ### UPDATE 7 - 2026-10-13 - Explosions and sparks - Ships explode when they lose a life: pixel particles in all directions plus five pieces of the hull that spin away and fade out. - Sparks fly when a ship is hit and when it crashes into a wall. The harder the crash, the more sparks. - Fixed shots and missiles that could fly straight through thin walls. ### UPDATE 6 - 2026-10-13 - Music and sound - The seven sound effects from the Amiga original are in the game: cannon, missile, guided missile, explosion, wall crash, ship against ship and cannon hit. - Title music and a live equalizer on the title screen and in the menu. - Options: music and sound effects can be switched on and off. ### UPDATE 5 - 2026-10-13 - Rounds and game modes - Rounds: play several rounds in a match (default 3). The last ship flying wins a round. - Results screen after the last round with rematch or main menu. A rematch lets you pick new ships. - Game Modes menu with Classic and Astro Duel. Astro Duel is playable, Race and Capture the Bratwurst are on the way. ### UPDATE 4 - 2026-10-13 - Maps and map editor - Three maps: the original arena (Sirius Bratwurst) and two remixes (Kepler Chorizo, Proxima Merguez). Pick the map in the menu. - Map editor: draw solid walls and boxes with the mouse, place start positions and save your own maps. New maps get a random name (a star or planet plus a sausage). - Every wall object has its own colour from the colour theme. ### UPDATE 3 - 2026-10-13 - Ships and weapons - Ships can collide with each other and knock each other away. A boosting ship hits much harder. - Every player has a unique colour from the theme, on the ship and on the player panel. - Switch special weapon and weapon position during a match, with the left trigger (weapon) and left bumper (weapon position). - Player panels along the bottom of the screen show energy, ammo, lives, special weapon and the weapon position. ### UPDATE 2 - 2026-10-13 - Terminal look - New menus in a terminal style: title screen, main menu, ship select and the match screen. - 30 dark colour themes (Base16) and a choice of accent colour. Settings are saved in files next to the game. - Sharp text at every resolution, a wide playfield option, scanlines and glow. - Players can join on the ship select screen, up to four. *The rest of this readme is on GitHub.*

🚀 Mousiki PlusOne — what's new

Changes made on top of Mousiki Plus in this fork, newest first.
The same list ships as plusone_changelog.txt.

📅 2026-10-25

⌨️ Keys: playback
New default keys (Settings → REFERENCE → Playback). All of them can be rebound as before.
ActionNew keyWas
Toggle Play / PauseSPACEp
Volume UpShift + ↑+
Volume DownShift + ↓-
Next TrackShift + →n
Prev TrackShift + ←b
  • Shift + arrow combinations can now be bound: press the combination in a key field, or type e.g. SHIFT+UP.
  • Where a shifted arrow is not bound it still acts as the plain arrow. The big list and queue overlays keep Shift + ↑/↓ for paging.
  • Radio Player: Shift + ↑/↓ changes the volume and Shift + →/← tunes the next / previous channel. The preset banks moved to Alt + ←/→.
🧭 Keys: navigation
New keys under Settings → REFERENCE → Navigation & View (also in the cheat sheet):
ActionKeyWhat it does
Fast Navigate UpPgUpjump 10 rows up
Fast Navigate DownPgDnjump 10 rows down
Navigate TopHomejump to the first row
Navigate BottomEndjump to the last row
  • They work in the track list and in the queue, can be rebound, and are stored in config.txt (HKeyNavigateFastUp, HKeyNavigateFastDown, HKeyNavigateTop, HKeyNavigateBottom).
  • ESC twice in a row (within 0.8 s) in the main view quits the program. The first ESC still goes back to the home view.
🔀 Play mode box
  • The box next to the search bar now shows the play mode as a word: LIST, REPEAT, SHUFFLE, STOP or QUEUE (queue then stop). M still steps through the modes.
  • The mode is saved at once and is back the next time Mousiki starts.
  • The sort mode chosen with Shift + T is remembered: it stays when you change folder, filter or search, and is back the next time Mousiki starts.
  • Next Track follows the play mode: with SHUFFLE on it jumps to a random track. The queue still plays in order.
📁 Folders pane (Music Player)
F6 swaps the QUEUE pane for a FOLDERS pane, F7 brings the queue back. The last choice is remembered (plusone_state.txt next to config.txt). The FOLDERS pane is a small file explorer over the local music paths (Settings → PATHS → Local Path):
  • Only folders with music files in them or below them are listed, with the number of files in each.
  • At the top level an All row comes first. It is not a folder: ENTER on it lists every track of all the paths. It is only there at the top.
  • ENTER on a folder lists the music files lying directly in it in the LOCAL AUDIO FILES pane. If the folder holds more folders, the pane goes into it and shows those (a > marks such a folder).
  • BACKSPACE goes one step back; at the top level the paths themselves are shown.
  • TAB moves the keys between the track list and the FOLDERS pane. Up, Down, PgUp, PgDn, Home and End work as in the lists.
🖥️ Modes and screens
  • F1 / F2 / F3 jump straight to the Music Player / Radio Player / Audio Book Player. A mode that is switched off under Settings → ON/OFF → MODES is skipped with a short note.
  • F4 opens the help wizard, F5 opens the settings.
  • A key legend now fills the bottom row, in the colours of the player, with the current mode highlighted:
    F1 music · F2 radio · F3 books · F4 wizard · F5 settings · F6 folders · F7 queue · ESC quit
    It is shown in all three players. F6 / F7 only exist in the Music Player.
  • Hold F12 (F12 controls in the right corner) and the legend shows the playback keys while the key is down:
    SPACE play · S← prev track · S→ next track · S↑ volume up · S↓ volume down · M mode · S+T sort · F11 fullscreen
    Their key boxes use another theme colour than the usual ones, and the F12 box itself a third one, so it is clear that other keys are showing. Let go and the normal legend is back. (Windows only; it is a hint about the default keys.)
  • Started with mousiki.cmd or lala.cmd (not mousiki-wt.cmd) the legend names these keys after F12 (F12↑, F12← ...) so they are unique.
  • F12 also works as Shift: hold F12 and press ↑/↓ for volume, ←/→ for previous / next track, T for sort, and so on.
🪟 Window and launchers
  • Portable folder Mousiki-Plus with the three launchers mousiki.cmd, mousiki-wt.cmd and lala.cmd. mousiki-wt.cmd opens Windows Terminal in a roughly square window (100 × 48 characters by default).
  • The window size is remembered. When Mousiki quits it saves the size to window_size.txt next to the launchers, and mousiki-wt.cmd opens the next window in that size.
  • Maximized and full screen are remembered too (window_state.txt). The normal size from before is kept, so leaving maximized brings it back.
  • Closing the window with the X button does not save the size; quit with the keys.
  • Old console window: mousiki.cmd / lala.cmd in cmd.exe have no font with Braille characters, so the disk and visualizers showed as boxes. Mousiki now notices this and draws block characters instead (coarser, same shapes). Windows Terminal, VS Code and ConEmu keep the Braille look. MOUSIKI_BLOCKS=1 / 0 forces blocks / Braille.
  • Alacritty: mousiki-alacritty.cmd starts Mousiki in Alacritty, a fast terminal that needs no installation (a portable alacritty.exe v0.17.0 with its licence files sits in the alacritty folder). No scroll bar, real Braille dots, remembers the window size and maximized / full screen, F11 toggles full screen. Needs Windows 10 1809 or later.
  • The program now finds the window of whichever terminal it runs in, so holding F12 and the saved window size also work in Alacritty and other terminals.
  • Full width: the screen used to stop at 200 columns and leave an empty strip on the right; it now goes up to 400 columns in all three players.
Mousiki is a terminal music player that was originally built for macOS/Linux by the amazing [itzender5820/mousiki, v1.0](https://github.com/itzender5820/mousiki) for people who prefer control, simplicity, and a keyboard (mousi-**key**). This Mousiki fork lets it also run natively on Windows (including quite a bunch of modifications and additions; code grew 6-7x the original length; design maintained for obvious reasons). All credits for the design, main feature set, and the core code goes to the original author. Since v2.5.0 the code base builds natively on **Linux and macOS** again (see [Build it yourself (Linux / macOS)](#build-it-yourself-linux--macos) or use the [setup packages or portable versions for all three platforms in the latest release](https://github.com/StSchwerdtfeger/mousiki-plus/releases/latest)). Windows remains the primary and most tested platform (only tested Linux via WSL and works fine so far, a few bugs were recently fixed; not much tested for macOS and non-WSL Linux systems). Feel free to give feedback in the discussions and report issues you might experience using this modified port. Build yourself (see [prerequisites](#prerequisites-windows) below) **or use the installer/portable (x64) version** that is included in every new release (since v2.1.0). A full **[user manual](Mousiki_User_Manual/Mousiki_User_Guide.md)** (also as [PDF](Mousiki_User_Manual/Mousiki_User_Guide.pdf)) walks through every entry of the in-app cheat sheet, every settings tab and every overlay. This fork exists because the original targets POSIX (Linux/macOS/Termux) and had no Windows build path at all. The Windows build uses no WSL, no MSYS runtime, no POSIX emulation layer, just a plain `mousiki.exe` built against the Win32 API and WASAPI. All Windows-specific code is guarded by `_WIN32`, so the very same sources also build on Linux (PulseAudio/PipeWire/ALSA) and macOS (CoreAudio) with the included `setup.sh`. Porting the original repository surfaced a long list of platform differences beyond the obvious ones (see [What had to change](Changes_from_the_Original.md#what-had-to-change-for-the-windows-port) in the separate file *Changes from the Original*), plus a small number of pre-existing bugs in the original codebase that had nothing to do with Windows and got fixed along the way. Along the Win32 port, **a lot of minor and major additions were made too**. The major ones are a e.g. **radio player mode**, **audio book mode**, **playlist menu** to create playlists from local (or downloaded) tracks, a **meta data editor** including **fetching artist/title via AcoustID/MusicBrainz** (audio fingerprinting done via chromaprint), a **listening history** (incl. the ability to add top tracks to the playback queue), an **XY/YT mode ASCII-Braille / full res. image oscilloscope and Audacity style spectrogram** as an alternative to the lyrics ball and lyrics, a **10 band EQ with 12 presets** and the ability to create and save custom presets, enlarged **list/queue overlays**, **sleep timer**, a **user manual** (.md and .pdf)... Minor changes/additions are e.g. a general key to shuffle to a next title (before only the next title in the list was possible or switching to shuffle mode), stereo audio playback and loudness normalization, adding paths via the settings menu, toggling the lyrics on/off via a hotkey command, an optimized search engine for Windows (searching meta data was very slow and only available 2-3 min. after starting the app), fuzzy search (e.g. "X-Files" didn't show up when searching "X Files" without the dash), a categorized cheat sheet... As mentioned, the design remained the same for obvious reasons; the design assets added are a Braille-ASCII music cassette, shown when no track is loaded, different volume bar symbols (one version acting like the changing ASCII pattern on the disk) and the default image in the audio book player... See [Changes from the Original](Changes_from_the_Original.md#added-features-beyond-the-port) for a full detailed list of modifications and added features, and [Features at a glance](#features-at-a-glance) below for an overview with screenshots. The latest larger feature additions are the mentioned **[radio player mode](#radio-player)** (online radio with a tuning-dial look, presets, Radio Browser search, recording option and its own listening history) and an **[audio book player mode](#audio-book-player)** (books and chapters, showing cover images, auto-marks, bookmarks, notes you write while you listen, chapter marks and cutting of long files, its own look and settings), both part of the very same program: press `SHIFT` and `+` (the `*` character) to go to the next mode (music player → radio → audio books) and `SHIFT` and `-` to go back; the order and the modes that are on are set in the settings. The radio is closed completely when you leave it, while the player and the audio book player only wait in the background (playback paused), so coming back to them is instant. - **Original:** [github.com/itzender5820/mousiki](https://github.com/itzender5820/mousiki) — ender ([itzender5820](https://github.com/itzender5820)) - **License:** Apache 2.0 — see [LICENSE](LICENSE) - **Windows port:** Steffen Schwerdtfeger ([StSchwerdtfeger](https://github.com/StSchwerdtfeger)), ported and adjusted with the help of AI tools (at first free chat versions, mostly Sonnet 5.5 set on medium and for some time MiMo V2.6; later also Claude with file and build tools in a sandbox, never on my own computer), then continuously adjusted, extended, tested, and debugged by me. I am not a professional developer of applications like this and I do not fully understand every detail of the original C++ code, but I had a lot of fun thinking my way into it and learned a lot (usually doing more data science / math coding and AI in such an extent makes little sense for me in the context of science). So far it took me around 180h over the last weeks to port it to Windows, design and add new features, test and debug (obsessively and escapistically spent my free time on it and just fell in love with the original design by itzender5820). The code quality seems good so far (from the feedback I got and my own evaluation, as far as I am capable of judging it), but there is surely room to optimize it, and reviews are welcome. So far I mostly smoothed the code to be more readable and similar to each other in general. The code is also scanned by CodeQL and tested via various test workflows, I added dependabot and weekly check on updates on the smaller third_party software that comes directly with Mousiki Plus. See the [Dependencies and security](#dependencies-and-security)chapter further below. *In general, a huge shout out for the great work by itzender5820 for this beautiful music player.* <3 It's the best and most fun music player I ever found. Makes me want to listen to music all the time :D

Again, feel free to give feedback in the discussions, report issues you might experience using this modified port or contributing in any other way... ## Features at a glance Everything below is in the current version (v4.6.0) and works the same on Windows, Linux and macOS but was only tested on Windows and WSL. The **[user manual](Mousiki_User_Manual/Mousiki_User_Guide.md)** describes every key and every setting; inside the app `?` opens the cheat sheet, `<` (German keyboard; `SHIFT+,` on an English one) a list of all menus and overlays to choose from, and `SHIFT+w` the help wizard. All pictures of this README are in the folder **[readme_images/](readme_images/)**. ### Music player

- **Local library** from as many folders as you like (MP3, FLAC, WAV, ALAC, M4A, OGG, OPUS, AAC, tracker modules, console and C64 music ...), sorted by folder, title, artist or length, with **fuzzy search** over file names and tags (`/` and the prefixes `/a:` artist, `/r:` ... ). - **Online:** search, stream and **download** from YouTube, SoundCloud and Bandcamp (yt-dlp), whole YouTube playlists in one go (bulk add), with a shared download archive. - **Queue** with lock, undo and "save as playlist", big list / folder / queue overlays, play modes list, repeat, shuffle, stop and queue-then-stop, and a shuffle-next key. - **Meta data panel** with the spinning braille disk, waveform progress bar, spectrum bars and the dummy buttons of the original design. - **Album covers** in the disk's place (Settings → ON/OFF → *Album Cover*, off by default): the picture inside the audio file or a picture in its folder whose name is close to the track's title or album (a fuzzy match, so one folder can hold the covers of several albums), shown as a real image in Kitty / Sixel terminals (braille dots otherwise): just the cover, the cover under the disk's moving gradient, or the grey cover in full resolution **behind the turning disk**, whose braille dots become pinholes the cover shines through (also with the dots themselves turning, or with the disk's full animation, the dots that come and go); the phone remote shows the cover too. Folder pictures can be jpg, png, webp, bmp, gif, tiff, avif, heic, jxl and more. *Cover Contrast* adds contrast to the picture, *Cover Search* sets where to look first (file or folder, or only one of them; any picture in the folder is the last resort). | | |:---:| |
**Just Cover** | |
**Cover with Gradient** | |
**Cover behind Disk** | ### Visualizations

- **Oscilloscope** in braille or as a real picture (Kitty / Sixel terminals): XY, YT and both together, a CRT beam with afterglow for **oscilloscope music**, grid, metrics and many tuning rows (`SHIFT+o`); full screen (`=`) and its own window (`)`). - **Creator** (`^`): turns a text into sound – **oscilloscope music** that draws the text on the XY scope, or a **spectrogram sound** that plays it as notes of a musical scale (so it always sounds pleasant) – saved as a WAV, played in a looping full-screen preview, and listed under *Created files* to open again. The folder with creations is excluded from the library scan, since at the oscilloscope version don't sound pleasent :D A second mode shows your **microphone live** (spectrogram or oscilloscope XY / YT, grid optional) and records it with `ENTER`. - **Spectrogram** in the field, over the whole screen (`SHIFT+u`) and in its own window (`(`), with its own options (`SHIFT+i`). - **Lyric sphere** and **spectrum bars**; the visualization field cycles with `.`.

### Lyrics and Karaoke mode - **Synchronized lyrics** fetched for local and online tracks, word-by-word animations, a timing editor for the offset (`ALT+L`), several versions kept per song.

- **Read lyrics** with **translations** (`CTRL+L`) and a full-screen **karaoke mode** with big braille letters (also Japanese, Chinese and Korean). - **Karaoke mode** open via `k`.

### Playlists, meta data, history, conversion - **Playlist editor** (`SHIFT+p`): create and edit playlists from local or downloaded tracks (library sortable with `SHIFT+t`, `/f:` searches folders), import and export M3U / M3U8.

- **Meta data editor** (`SHIFT+m`): edit tags, rename files, and **fetch missing tags by audio fingerprint** (AcoustID / MusicBrainz) for one title or a whole list.

- **File conversion** between audio formats. - **Listening history** (`SHIFT+h`): history, top tracks, top playlists and listening habits, plus **smart lists** to queue (top 25 of the week, by time of day ...). ### Sound - **10-band equalizer** with 12 presets and your own presets, **loudness normalization**, stereo / mono, a **sleep timer**.

### Radio player The radio is part of the same program: `*` (`SHIFT` and `+` on a German keyboard, `SHIFT+8` on an English one) goes to the next mode, `_` (`SHIFT` and `-`) to the previous one. - An **ON AIR / OFF AIR sign** with a colour wave, a tuning-dial frequency band, its own oscilloscope, spectrogram and equalizer. - **Radio Browser** search through tens of thousands of stations, **16 presets** in several preset lists, **station lists**, a big stations overlay. - **Timeshift** (pause, jump back, back to live), **recording** (also from the past buffer), its own **listening history**, and finding the current song on YouTube to download it.

### Audio book player The audio book player is the third mode, switched to with the same key as to the other modes (`SHIFT` and `+`; `SHIFT` and `-` goes back). **Settings → ON/OFF → MODES** switches modes off (one always stays on) and changes their order; **Settings → PATHS → AUDIO BOOK PATH** is the folder of your books (shown in every mode). Files/folders placed there wont show up in the music player mode... *The rest of this readme is on GitHub.*

# musikcube

a cross-platform, terminal-based audio engine, library, player and server written in c++.

musikcube compiles and runs easily on windows, macos and linux. it also runs well on a raspberry pi with raspbian, and can be setup as a streaming audio server.

check out the [installation guide](https://github.com/clangen/musikcube/wiki/installing) to get up and running.

be sure to also read through a [the user guide](https://github.com/clangen/musikcube/wiki/user-guide), which describes app's navigation paradigm and lists all the default keyboard shortcuts.

if you want to build it from source, [the instructions are here](https://github.com/clangen/musikcube/wiki/building).

# screenshots

it looks something like this on windows:

![windows screenshot](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/clangen/clangen-projects-static/master/musikcube/screenshots/windows.png)

and this on macos:

![osx screenshot](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/clangen/clangen-projects-static/master/musikcube/screenshots/osx.png)

and on linux:

![linux screenshot](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/clangen/clangen-projects-static/master/musikcube/screenshots/linux.png)

here's a demo (made with asciinema):

[![asciicast](https://asciinema.org/a/129748.png)](https://asciinema.org/a/129748)

while the main musikcube app runs in the console, you can also stream audio from (and even remote control) musikcube using the `musikdroid` android app, which can be downloaded in the `releases` section above. it looks like this:

![android screenshot](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/clangen/clangen-projects-static/master/musikcube/screenshots/android.png)

# installation

binaries are available in the [releases](https://github.com/clangen/musikcube/releases) page.

while macos binaries are provided, you can also install via homebrew as follows:

- `brew install musikcube`

on freebsd musikcube can be installed as follows:

- `pkg install musikcube`

on openbsd musikcube can be installed as follows:

- `pkg_add install musikcube`

on windows, you can install via chocolatey:

- `choco install musikcube`

then run using shell, Win+R dialog or by typing in Start Menu `musikcube` or `mcube`.

# raspberry pi

musikcube runs well on a raspberry pi, connected to your home stereo. [see here for detailed setup instructions](https://github.com/clangen/musikcube/wiki/raspberry-pi).

# compiling

if you'd like to compile the project yourself, you can check out the [build instructions](https://github.com/clangen/musikcube/wiki/building).

# keyboard shortcuts

a list of all keyboard shortcuts can be found in the [user guide](https://github.com/clangen/musikcube/wiki/user-guide)

# streaming server

musikcube ships with a streaming audio server enabled by default. it runs a websocket server on port 7905, used for metadata retrieval. an http server runs on port 7906, and is used to serve (optionally transcoded) audio data to clients.

**it's important to understand that, out of the box, the server (and remote api) should NOT be considered safe for use outside of a local network**. the websockets service only supports a simple password challenge, and the audio http server just handles Basic authorization. it does not provide ssl or tls. the server also stores the password in plain text in a settings file on the local machine.

you can fix some of this using a reverse proxy to provide ssl termination. details in the [ssl-server-setup section](https://github.com/clangen/musikcube/wiki/ssl-server-setup). while this improves things, you should exercise caution exposing these services over the internet.

if you're interested in writing your own frontend, [api documentation is available here](https://github.com/clangen/musikcube/wiki/remote-api-documentation).

# sdk

the musikcube sdk is a set of small, pure-virtual c++ classes and a handful of enums and constants. they're still in the process of being slimmed down. you can see what they currently look like here: https://github.com/clangen/musikcube/tree/master/src/musikcore/sdk

projects.readme:
# Wipeout XL / 2097

This project is a rewrite of Wipeout XL / 2097 inspired by [wipeout-rewrite](https://github.com/phoboslab/wipeout-rewrite). It is based off a decompilation of the PS1 version of Wipeout XL & 2097 and another partial decompilation of the PC release.

The goal of this project is to keep the original behavior as much as possible while also upgrading the game with more capabilities. Here is a rough list of the changes in this game compared with the original PS1 version:
- Higher resolutions (HD Mod support, accurate rendering w/out PGXP)
- Uncapped framerates (physics & game logic still limited to original framerate)
- Widescreen support
- Split-screen for one on one mode
- Loading in Wipeout and Wipeout 64 tracks (this won't be perfect but it works pretty well right now)
- Higher render distance (configurable if you prefer older style)
- Custom music
- Touch controls for mobile and web (WIP)
- Autosave & converting save files
- Minor culling & depth buffer fixes

If you would like to change any of the settings or files for the game press the <kbd>`</kbd> or <kbd>~</kbd> key on your keyboard to toggle the debug UI. It has multiple tabs with many options to configure.

## Getting Started

To play this game, you will need a copy of Wipeout XL or Wipeout 2097. Store it somewhere on your computer.

If you are on Windows & macOS, you can download the latest build from the Releases and select your .cue file or archive of your PS1 rom when the app or exe prompts you for your game files. Users on all other platforms will have to [build](#build) the launcher themselves.

## SLOP LINE - Everything below this line is autogenerated

The PlayStation game (USA, SCUS-94351) running natively on macOS, Linux and
Windows, and in a web browser. One code base builds all four (the same game, the
same platform layer over SDL3 and OpenGL; the web uses WebGL 2). The game is the console's own code: the decompiled C of the retail
executable, compiled for the PC, with the PlayStation libraries replaced by the
platform layer (OpenGL drawing at any resolution, the sound chip, the CD drive,
pads and memory cards). It plays like the console, frame for frame: see
[docs/LOCKSTEP.md](docs/LOCKSTEP.md) for the comparison with recordings of the
real game.

## What you need

- Your copy of the PlayStation disc (Wipeout XL USA, or WipEout 2097 Europe):
  a `.cue` with its `.bin` tracks, a `.bin` without its `.cue`, or an archive
  of either (`.7z`, `.zip`, `.rar`, `.tar`, `.gz` and the like). The music
  plays from the disc's audio tracks, the intro and ending movies from its
  movie files.
- To build: CMake, Ninja, a C compiler (Clang or GCC), and SDL3 3.2 or later
  (zlib for the test traces is optional). Where CMake does not find SDL3 it
  downloads and builds it (`-DWIPEOUT_BUILD_SDL=ON` always does). The same
  goes for libarchive (`libarchive-dev` on Linux, Homebrew's `libarchive` on
  macOS; `-DWIPEOUT_BUILD_LIBARCHIVE=ON` always builds it).

## Build

Each build has its own folder under `build/`. macOS (Homebrew's `sdl3`):

```sh
cmake -S . -B build/mac -G Ninja -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=RelWithDebInfo
ninja -C build/mac
```

It also makes `build/mac/Wipeout XL.app`, with the Mac version's icon and the
Homebrew libraries it uses inside (copy it to `/Applications`).

Linux (for example Debian 13 or Ubuntu 25.04: `libsdl3-dev libgl-dev`): the
same two commands with `build/linux`.

Windows, with MSYS2's MinGW-w64 (UCRT64 or CLANG64 shell, packages `cmake`
`ninja` `gcc` or `clang`): the same two commands with `build/windows`. From
macOS or Linux, with the MinGW-w64 cross compiler, use the toolchain file:

```sh
cmake -S . -B build/windows -G Ninja -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
      -DCMAKE_TOOLCHAIN_FILE=cmake/mingw-w64-x86_64.cmake
ninja -C build/windows
```

`wipeoutxl.exe` is a single file, with SDL3 and the C runtime linked in and the
PC version's icon.

The web, with Emscripten:

```sh
emcmake cmake -S . -B build/web -G Ninja -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
      -DWIPEOUT_WEB_DISC="path/to/Wipeout XL (USA).cue"
ninja -C build/web
```

This makes `wipeoutxl.html`, `wipeoutxl.js` and `wipeoutxl.wasm`, and, as
wipeout-rewrite's web build has its data beside the page, the disc the page
loads by itself: `WIPEOUT_WEB_DISC` (your own copy) links the `.cue` and its
`.bin` tracks into `build/web/disc/` and writes `wipeoutxl-data.json`, which
names it. Put `build/web` on any web server with the links followed
(`cp -RL build/web site`), or try it with `python3 -m http.server` in
`build/web` and open `http://localhost:8000/wipeoutxl.html`. A host can also
put a disc there by hand: `disc/Wipeout XL (USA).cue` with its tracks is found
without a `wipeoutxl-data.json`, and the JSON (`{ "disc": "url/of/the.cue" }`)
can point anywhere on the site. With `-DWIPEOUT_WEB_DISC_MUSIC=OFF` only the
data track goes into `disc/` (about 86 MB in place of about 700): the game
plays, without its music.

## Phones and tablets (iOS, Android)

The same game runs on iPhone, iPad and Android, landscape and full screen (OpenGL ES 3), with touch controls
(below) and widescreen on from the start. SDL3 and libarchive are downloaded and built into the app.

iOS (Xcode; the simulator needs no signing):

```sh
cmake -S . -B build/ios -G Ninja -DCMAKE_SYSTEM_NAME=iOS -DCMAKE_OSX_SYSROOT=iphonesimulator \
      -DCMAKE_OSX_ARCHITECTURES=arm64 -DCMAKE_OSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET=15.0 -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=RelWithDebInfo
ninja -C build/ios wipeoutxl
codesign --force --sign - "build/ios/Wipeout XL.app"
xcrun simctl install booted "build/ios/Wipeout XL.app"
```

For a device, configure with `-G Xcode -DCMAKE_SYSTEM_NAME=iOS -DWIPEOUT_IOS_TEAM=<your team id>
-DWIPEOUT_IOS_BUNDLE_ID=<an id of yours>`, open the project in Xcode and run it on the device (the first
configure takes a while: Xcode checks every one of libarchive's tests). Put the disc image (the `.cue` with its
`.bin` files, or a `.zip`/`.7z` of them) in the Files app, On My iPhone (or iPad) > Wipeout XL; the game finds
it there, or says where to put it.

Android (the Android SDK with NDK 28 and Gradle 8 with JDK 17 or 21; `platform/android`):

```sh
cd platform/android
gradle assembleDebug        # app/build/outputs/apk/debug/app-debug.apk
adb install -r app/build/outputs/apk/debug/app-debug.apk
```

At the first start the game looks for the disc image in its folder on the device's storage
(`Android/data/com.example.wipeoutxl/files`, reached from a computer over USB, or `adb push`); without one
it asks, and "Choose files..." picks the `.cue` with its `.bin` files (or a `.zip`/`.7z`) with the system's
picker and copies them in. On both, the debug console (the button at the top left) changes the disc later; the
new one is used from the next start. The two-player link modes need a second program, which a phone cannot
start: they find no partner, as on the web.

## Debug console

The ~ key (below Esc) opens a console over the whole game window: frame rates and a
frame-rate overlay, the draw distance (the console's or the whole track) and
its fade, the frame rate, widescreen, the resolution, HD textures, skipping the intro movie and the start-up logos, full screen, the
frame recorder (off by default; up to 240 pictures a second, the ones between the game's frames too; Tab: the last 3 seconds, or from one Tab to the next, with every
primitive behind any pixel; while recording, its frames come in as they are drawn, `,` and `.` step back and
forward a frame, and − / + zoom the picture, kept at the resolution it was drawn at), and where the settings and the memory cards are. Changes are saved at once to
`wipeoutxl.ini` in the user's data folder; a new saves folder takes effect at
the next start. Dear ImGui (`platform/third_party/imgui`, MIT) draws it.

## How it is built

[docs/PLAN.md](docs/PLAN.md) describes the design; [docs/IO.md](docs/IO.md)
the sound, CD, pad and card side.

projects.summary: Psychopomp: The Pure and the Perished
projects.readme:
# PSYCHOPOMP

**Psychopomp** is a 2-player tactical board-game/battle game inspired by the classic *Archon: The Light and the Dark*.

The central structure remains:

1. Two players control opposing teams of creatures.
2. Players take turns moving creatures on a board.
3. Capturing a creature starts a battle.
4. A battle is resolved through a Yahtzee-like dice allocation phase followed by a real creature-vs-creature fight.
5. Captured power points and creature elimination determine victory.
6. A surviving creature keeps its remaining HP after the battle.

The first implementation targets **PC** and **browser**, with offline play and itch.io distribution. The project must be designed so the game rules and content are independent from the rendering/input/platform layer, allowing future ports to systems such as Linux, macOS, Switch, Game Boy Color, NES and C64.

## Design pillars

- **Archon-like strategic board layer**
- **Dice-driven preparation instead of the original direct combat setup**
- **Real-time creature combat after preparation**
- **Persistent surviving HP**
- **Data-driven creatures**
- **Built-in creature/content editor**
- **Offline-first**
- **Two local players**
- **Gamepad + keyboard**
- **Browser build**
- **itch.io-ready**
- **Deterministic, portable game rules**
- **No mandatory online service**

## Important terminology

| Term | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Board | The tactical grid on which creatures move |
| Creature | A playable monster/unit |
| Power Point | One of the five capturable strategic locations |
| Battle | The combat sequence triggered when one creature attacks another |
| Dice Phase | The pre-battle Yahtzee-like allocation phase |
| Stat Slot | A category receiving one or more dice |
| Special | A creature-specific ability activated by satisfying dice requirements |
| Persistent HP | HP remaining after battle and carried into later battles |
| Roster | The creatures available to a player |
| Content Pack | A collection of creature definitions and assets |
| Editor | The built-in tool for creating/testing creature content |

## Project rule

The implementation must never hard-code individual creatures into combat logic.

A creature should be defined as data:

- identity
- artwork
- HP
- movement
- combat stats
- dice allocation rules
- special ability
- optional visual/audio metadata

This makes the game easier to balance and makes the eventual retro ports much more realistic.

See:

- `GAME_DESIGN.md`
- `RULES.md`
- `COMBAT.md`
- `CONTENT.md`
- `EDITOR.md`
- `ARCHITECTURE.md`
- `UI.md`
- `CONTROLS.md`
- `PORTABILITY.md`
- `TESTING.md`
- `CLAUDE_CODE.md`
- `ROADMAP.md`

## Getting started (vertical slice 0.1)

Requires Node.js 20+. Only dev tools are installed (vite, typescript, vitest); the game has no runtime dependencies.

## Development

```text
npm install
npm run dev        # Vite prints the local URL (served under /Psychopomp/)
```

## Test

```text
npm test           # core test suite (headless)
npm run typecheck
npm run build      # static build in dist/
```

## Production preview

```text
npm run preview    # serves dist/ at http://localhost:4173/Psychopomp/
```

## GitHub Pages

Live build: https://thermoptic.github.io/Psychopomp/

Every push to `main` runs `.github/workflows/deploy.yml` (npm ci → npm test → npm run build → deploy `dist/`).
The Vite `base` is `/Psychopomp/` because this is a GitHub Pages project site. Pages is only hosting:
the game, its content and all assets are bundled into the build and need no backend or external service.

## Developer editor (/editor)

Internal content tool, not part of the player UI: `npm run dev` then open `/Psychopomp/editor/`.
MONSTERS (identity, health, P1/P2, 9×9 position, start modifiers, Special slot conditions, Powerup) and
POWERUPS (melee/ranged settings on 1-10 scales). Saved content lives in this browser and is used by new
matches; EXPORT/IMPORT move items as versioned JSON files (see `src/content/saveFormat.ts`).

Code layout and the assumptions made for this slice: see `IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md`.
Content lives in `content/packs/base/` (ruleset, board, creatures as JSON).

projects.description:
Rebooted with modern improvements and new features.
Originally released in 2011, 0Space returns with bugfixes and quality of life upgrades. 0Space is a local multiplayer deathmatch for 2–4 players, set in a zero-gravity environment. Move freely across floors, walls, and ceilings, or launch yourself into open space and drift between surfaces. The camera rotates with the environment, allowing combat to unfold in every direction.

Each match consists of a series of levels where kills earn points and deaths deduct them. A single hit is enough to eliminate an opponent, making positioning and movement essential to survival.

Created by Beau Blyth for the 2011 TIGSource Versus Competition, 0Space was inspired by the zero-gravity Battle Room in Orson Scott Card's novel Ender's Game.



In 2026 Thermoptic took over the project and updated the game. The goal was to make 0Space run well on modern Windows while keeping the feel of the original exactly as it was. The original release can have problems on current Windows versions: crashes, poor speed and replays that do not work. This version was rebuilt from the original release's data with the help of AI and compiled in GameMaker Studio 1.4, and every change was tested against the way the original plays.

- Crash Fixes, freezes and slow-downs of the original.
- Working replays, working title demos, music and all sound effects.
- Controller support for all four players on modern gamepads (XInput)

- Widescreen support, you can still enable 4:3 in the Options menu.
- New Pause menu (Restart Match, Options, Controls and Quit)
- Countdown timer at the start of every round and after you resume from pause.
- A dedicated Sword Button (Y on a gamepad).
- Games Modes! Classic and the new Reboot Mode
- Powerups! Crates that spawn during a round, with four different weapons.
- 4 New levels added.
- Flux Generator! Procedurally generated levels: every round builds a brand-new map, so no two matches play the same.
- Analogue Aim! Aim in any direction using the analogue stick. Dont worry, the original digital aim is still there.
- Crt Filters. Four old-TV looks for more arcade vibes.
- And more! Read the readme.txt and changes.txt for more info

0Space and all of its original game design, art, levels and music belong to their creators. This version is an unofficial, non-commercial fan update, made out of love for the game. Original game Beau Blyth (Teknopants). Copyright 2011-2014. Original music Max Coburn. Gravity Reboot version: Updated and extended by Thermoptic, 2026.

projects.readme:
Popamp Deluxe

## What's new in Popamp Deluxe *Updated 2026-11-22. The same list, as a text file that comes with every download: [popampdeluxe.txt](popampdeluxe.txt).* - **Palettes** (Skin Browser > Palette). Forty dark Base16 schemes, with *Original* at the top. Pick one, or walk through the list with the arrow keys, and every vector skin is recoloured in the player at once: dark base00 surfaces, base0E title-bar lines, base0B lamps, base05 text.

- **Hotkeys** (Preferences > Hotkeys). Every keyboard shortcut is listed and can be changed, added to, cleared or reset. Kept in `popamp.ini`. - **Groups in the Foldertree.** Organise the folders of the left list in groups that fold in and out, and edit them in the Folder and Group Editor (LIST button > Folders and groups). Kept in `popamp.ini`. - **Preferences in the skin's own title bar.** The window uses the skin's windowshade strip instead of the system's title bar. - **Apply button** in Preferences: OK without closing the window. - **Line spacing** (Preferences > Interface). Set the space between the lines of text in the playlist and the Media Library; 0 is the closest, 5 the default. - **Hide file extension** (Preferences > Media Library) and an icon of its own for playlist files in the Foldertree. - **Playlist files in the Foldertree**. .m3u/.pls files show in the right list; double-click adds all their songs to the playlist. - **Copy to clipboard** (right-click in the playlist, Windows). Every song in the playlist is copied to the clipboard as files; press Ctrl+V in an Explorer folder to copy them there. - **Media Library Foldertree** (Preferences > Media Library). A second kind of library window: add folders on the left, browse them like Explorer on the right, by file name, sorted by title or date.

- **A custom font** (Preferences > Font). Pick any `.ttf` or `.otf` from the `fonts` folder and a size, for the playlist, library, menus and dialogs, or tick *Custom Skin Bmp Font* to write them with the letters of the skin's own `text.bmp`. - **Windowshade for the Media Library.** Double-click its title bar and it rolls up to a strip, as the main, equalizer and playlist windows do. - **Title-bar shortcuts** (Preferences > Shortcuts). Choose what a right click, a middle click or the mouse wheel on the title bar of the main, equalizer or playlist window does, in full size or windowshade mode: previous or next track, pause, stop, shuffle, repeat, volume up or down. Middle-click the equalizer to pause, or hover its title bar and scroll to change the volume, with no click needed.

- **A skin comes with the player.** `popamp-classified.psz` is in the `skins` folder with the program; it shows up in the Skin Browser. Popamp starts with its built-in skin. - **A `skins` folder beside the program.** Drop any `.wsz` in it and it shows up in the Skin Browser (Alt+S) at once, even while the browser is open. - **Volume and balance in the shaded equalizer,** as in Winamp.

Download · Features · Usage · Make a skin · Roadmap

Popamp is a desktop music player in the spirit of Winamp 2: a main window, a 10-band equalizer and a playlist that snap together, and a different look whenever you want one. It is written in Rust and runs on Linux and Windows. - **Sharp at any size.** Popamp's own skins are drawn as vectors, so they stay crisp from ×1 to ×3 in steps of a quarter, on any monitor. - **Thousands of classic skins.** Open any `.wsz` file, or browse, search and install skins from the [Winamp Skin Museum](https://skins.webamp.org) without leaving the player. - **A gallery in the player.** Install and update the skins and plug-ins from [popamp.app](https://popamp.app) in a click, each checked against the catalog. - **Sounds right.** Gapless playback, ReplayGain, a 10-band equalizer with `.eqf` presets, internet radio, and the common formats: MP3, AAC, FLAC, Ogg Vorbis, Opus, WAV, ALAC, MIDI, tracker modules and more. - **At home on your desktop.** Media keys and the system's player controls show the track and its cover. - **A player that is a bar.** In [toolbar mode](#toolbar-mode) the main window becomes a strip along the top or bottom of the screen, on Linux and Windows, with the room for it kept like a taskbar's. - **Plug-ins you allow.** Sandboxed WebAssembly plug-ins, each switched on by you: [YouTube](https://github.com/popamp/plugin-youtube) as a source, [Crossfeed](https://github.com/popamp/plugin-crossfeed) for headphones, [Monkey's Audio](https://github.com/popamp/plugin-ape) for `.ape` files. - **Your music stays yours.** No account, no cloud, no library to import: it plays files and the streams you open. ### Skins | [Default](https://github.com/popamp/popamp-skin-default) (built in) | [Steel](https://github.com/popamp/skin-steel) | [Modern](https://github.com/popamp/skin-modern) | |:---:|:---:|:---:| | | | | ### Toolbar mode The whole player in one strip along the bottom or top of the screen: transport, visualizer, clock, title, volume and the EQ and playlist switches, with the equalizer and the playlist above its right end. On Linux (X11) the strip is reserved with `_NET_WM_STRUT_PARTIAL`, so maximized windows stop at it as they do at a taskbar, and it keeps clear of the desktop's own panels; on Windows it is an application bar. Turn it on, move it and size it under Main menu > *Toolbar mode*. The built-in skin and the Modern, Steel, Classified and D11 skins each carry a bar beside their window, in all their colour sets. More in [features](docs/features.md#toolbar-mode). ## Why? Popamp began with a search for Winamp on a Linux desktop. Two good players written in Rust already existed, [Linamp](https://github.com/sayoojkkarun/linamp) and [Ferramp](https://github.com/SpankulatorX/ferramp), but both drew the classic bitmap skins, and on a modern monitor with the desktop scaled up those skins went soft and blurry, even at double size. So Popamp took Linamp's code, brought over the best of Ferramp's features, and added one new idea: skins drawn as vectors, sharp at any size, fractional ones included. Classic skins got the same care. Then came plug-ins that cannot reach more than you allow, and a Windows version, so one player and its skins work on both systems. ## Install Downloads are on the [Releases page](https://github.com/popamp/popamp/releases), and Debian, Ubuntu, openSUSE and Fedora can install it from a repository that keeps it up to date.
